solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Providing aid from stake money invested in silver (8)

indicatorNotes.invested in: money invested in something is put inside it, so BETTIN goes inside AG

blocks.note: a stake is a bet
tin is old slang for money
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Someone funds a good cause by putting their gambling winnings into silver.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stake money" reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces, BET and TIN. Silver's symbol AG then opens up around both.
annotation.definitionFit: Abetting someone is helping or encouraging them, usually in wrongdoing.

entries.clue: Something made a report extremely close to the truth (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: kept as it is
first and last letters of REPORT
last letter of THE
a fact is a truth

annotation.surface: A journalist files a story that comes very near to the truth.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close to the truth" reads as one idiom, but it splits: "close to the" gives E and "truth" is FACT on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any object shaped by human hands counts, which is all "something made" asks for.

entries.clue: Oslo’s latest new premium clothes store (8)

indicatorNotes.latest: the latest letter of a word is its last one
indicatorNotes.new: a new version of PREMIUM + O is a rearranged one

blocks.note: last letter of OSLO
anagram fodder with the O

annotation.surface: A smart new boutique has just opened in Oslo.
annotation.walkthrough: Oslo looks like a place the store is in, but it gives only its last letter to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop, and clothes stores are often given the name.
annotation.definitionNote: An emporium sells all sorts of goods; "clothes store" is one kind.

entries.clue: Yankee that’s annoying turning up late (5)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down answer, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
"drat!" is what you say when something annoys you

annotation.surface: An American's habit of arriving late is getting on someone's nerves.
annotation.walkthrough: "That's annoying" seems to describe the lateness, but it stands for the exclamation DRAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Tardy means slow to arrive, or late.

entries.clue: Spreading concern, few seen gathering briefing papers (4,10)

indicatorNotes.Spreading: spreading the letters around rearranges them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Worry spreads through a group while hardly anyone is seen gathering up important documents.
annotation.walkthrough: "Papers" here means newspapers: a news conference is a gathering that briefs the press.
annotation.definitionFit: At a news conference, reporters from the papers are briefed together.

entries.clue: Place to buy in or sell out (4)

blocks.note: a retail premises, the ordinary noun
to betray someone, as an informer does to the police; a British slang verb

annotation.surface: A trader's advice: buy stock when it is cheap, sell when it peaks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Buy in" and "sell out" look like opposite trades. In fact "sell out" means to betray, and "to shop" someone is British slang for informing on them.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the everyday noun for a retail premises, and British slang for informing on someone, which betrays them.

entries.clue: Suspended on railway for lacking sufficient fare (6)

blocks.note: hung means suspended
in a down answer, HUNG sits on top of RY
RY is an abbreviation for railway

annotation.surface: A passenger is thrown off the train for not having enough money for the ticket.
annotation.walkthrough: Fare as a train ticket fits the railway surface, but here it means food.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone without enough fare, or food, is hungry.

entries.clue: Quietly letting agreement bring happiness (6)

blocks.note: p (piano) means quietly in music
a lease is an agreement to let property

annotation.surface: Signing a tenancy without fuss makes everyone content.
annotation.walkthrough: "Letting" seems to mean allowing, but it means renting out property, so the agreement is a LEASE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb means to give someone pleasure or satisfaction.

entries.clue: Troops secured a row for snipers somehow (9,2,3)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters come together in some other way, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Soldiers have somehow won a line of positions for their marksmen.
annotation.walkthrough: "Secured" reads as an active verb, but in the definition it means held captive: these are troops who have been secured.
annotation.definitionFit: Prisoners of war are soldiers held captive by the enemy.

entries.clue: A squealer’s confession sounded sweet, but cold (3,5)

indicatorNotes.sounded: the confession is said, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: someone who squeals admits "I scream"

annotation.surface: An informer confesses in a voice that is sweet but chilly.
annotation.walkthrough: A squealer seems to be an informer, but it is just someone who screams. The old rhyme "I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream" plays on the same sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a frozen dessert, sugary yet chilled, and the "but" plays up that contrast.

entries.clue: Jersey artist of high standing (3,6)

blocks.note: a jersey is a top
someone who draws is a drawer

annotation.surface: A respected painter from the island of Jersey.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital J makes Jersey look like the Channel Island, but it is the sweater. A drawer is also where a jersey is kept.
annotation.definitionFit: Top drawer means of the highest social class or quality.

entries.clue: Boat staff bringing nothing on board (5)

indicatorNotes.on board: something on board is inside the vessel, so O goes inside CANE

blocks.note: a cane is a walking staff
O looks like zero

annotation.surface: The crew of a boat bring nothing with them.
annotation.walkthrough: Staff seems to mean the crew, but it is a stick, a CANE.
annotation.definitionFit: A canoe is a small, light boat paddled by hand.

entries.clue: Raid spanning a period of a year (5)

blocks.note: as in "for a year": for gives how long something lasts
kept as it is
Y is an abbreviation for year

annotation.surface: A military campaign that lasted twelve months.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue spells out the phrase "for a year", with "spanning a period of" standing in for FOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden attack or raid into enemy territory.

entries.clue: Car chase mostly prepared, DS means to get ready (4,5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of CHASE, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are made into something new, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: CAR CHASE without its last letter
used as printed; DS is a detective sergeant in the surface

annotation.surface: A detective sergeant gets ready for a car chase.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ready" means cash here, as in "ready money", so the definition is the means of getting cash. "Get ready" seems to mean prepare.
annotation.definitionFit: A cash card lets you take ready money from a machine.

entries.clue: Look back on gas sanctions (12)

indicatorNotes.back: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a countenance is a face or look
last letter of GAS, placed after

annotation.surface: Someone reflects on the sanctions placed on gas supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: "Look back on" seems to mean remember. Split it up: "Look" is COUNTENANCE and "back" takes the last letter of GAS.
annotation.definitionFit: To countenance something is to allow or approve it, so countenances means sanctions.

entries.clue: What’s up with MPs limiting speculation? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: THEORIES is plural; "speculation" is a mass noun covering the same thing.

indicatorNotes.up: in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.limiting: TORIES limit HE by enclosing it

blocks.note: Tories are Conservative MPs
"Eh?" means "What?", and it is written upwards

annotation.surface: A question about the talk going around among members of Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: "What's up" reads as "what's happening". Split it: "What" is EH and "'s up" turns it over. The Tories are Britain's Conservative party.
annotation.definitionFit: Theories are ideas not yet proved, which is what speculation offers.

entries.clue: Charge identified with electron (8)

blocks.note: a thing stamped is marked to show what it is
e is the symbol for an electron

annotation.surface: A physics fact: the charge that belongs to an electron.
annotation.walkthrough: Charge and electron together point to electricity. Here charge is the headlong rush of a herd.
annotation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass charge of animals or people.

entries.clue: State vessel used to rescue an elite force (8)

blocks.note: Noah's ark saved the animals from the flood
kept as it is
the SAS is the British Army's special forces regiment

annotation.surface: A government ship is sent to save a crack unit.
annotation.walkthrough: "State vessel" reads as a ship of state, but "State" is the definition. The rest of the clue describes the ark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the fifty US states, in the south of the country.

entries.clue: What newsreaders read in French, the expert seducer conceals (12)

indicatorNotes.conceals: TEMPTER hides LE PRO inside itself

blocks.note: a tempter is a seducer; "the expert" is split up, see below
le is French for the
a pro is an expert

annotation.surface: A French phrase about an accomplished seducer who hides what he's up to.
annotation.walkthrough: "The expert seducer" reads as one phrase, but "the" belongs with "in French" to give LE, and "expert" is PRO.
annotation.definitionFit: A teleprompter shows the script newsreaders read on camera.

entries.clue: Advantages of dogs off the lead (6)

indicatorNotes.off the lead: the lead is the first letter, and it comes off

blocks.note: basset hounds; the B goes

annotation.surface: The benefits of letting your dogs run loose.
annotation.walkthrough: A lead is a dog's leash in the surface, but in the wordplay it is the leading letter of BASSETS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a useful skill or quality counts in your favour, so it is an advantage.

entries.clue: Careful cutting a stem (6)

indicatorNotes.cutting: cutting A out removes it from the word

blocks.note: sparing means careful, as with money
the A removed from SPARING

annotation.surface: A gardener's advice to take care when pruning a stalk.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stem" looks like a noun, a plant stalk, but it is the verb, as in problems that stem from something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: trouble that stems from a cause can equally be said to arise from it.

entries.clue: Comic character from Peru: he’s funny or contrary (9)

indicatorNotes.funny: funny letters are strange ones, i.e. rearranged
indicatorNotes.contrary: contrary means going the other way, so OR reads backwards

blocks.note: anagram of PERU HES
OR backwards

annotation.surface: A cartoon figure from Peru who is either amusing or awkward.
annotation.walkthrough: "Comic character" seems to mean a funny man, but it is a character from a comic book.
annotation.definitionFit: Superheroes are the heroes of comic books.

entries.clue: Dance backwards while gripping a medic (5)

indicatorNotes.gripping: SA grips A MB between its letters

blocks.note: as = while, turned round
kept as it is
MB is a medical degree, so a doctor

annotation.surface: Someone dances backwards while holding on to a doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dance backwards" looks like a step in the dance. In fact "Dance" is the definition and "backwards" turns AS round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lively Brazilian dance, famous from the Rio carnival.

entries.clue: Something footballers put on skin (5)

blocks.note: a British football team's shirts, shorts and socks, its kit
a verb: to peel off an outer covering

annotation.surface: Players rub something into their skin before a match.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put on skin" reads like applying cream, but the clue breaks after "on". In Britain a football team's strip is its shirts, shorts and socks.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the British noun for a team's kit, and the verb for peeling off an outer layer, as you skin fruit.

entries.clue: Skip over some novel ideas (5)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of NOVEL IDEAS are used

blocks.note: found inside novEL IDEas

annotation.surface: An instruction to pass over a few fresh ideas.
annotation.walkthrough: "Novel" could be a book or an anagram signal, but here it just carries the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit or skip over, especially a sound in speech.

entries.clue: Striking people outside that hurt colleagues (2,7)

indicatorNotes.outside: CORKERS sits outside OW, enclosing it

blocks.note: a corker is a strikingly attractive person
"ow!" is what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: Workers on strike wound their fellow employees who cross the picket line.
annotation.walkthrough: "Striking people" suggests workers on strike, which suits the answer. It means corkers, a British word for people who look stunning.
annotation.definitionFit: Co-workers are people who work together: colleagues.

entries.clue: I’m exasperated seeing time being wasted (4)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a whole statement; SIGH is the sound that says it.

indicatorNotes.being wasted: the T is used up and lost

blocks.note: sight is the act of seeing
T for time, removed from SIGHT

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed to watch time frittered away.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole top and bottom rows make a pun: A BETTING SHOP / SIGH PROPHETS sounds like "a betting shop's high profits".
annotation.definitionFit: A sigh is the sound someone makes to show they are exasperated.

entries.clue: Forecasters for hours absorbed by “cats and dogs”? (8)

indicatorNotes.absorbed by: something absorbed by a thing is taken inside it, so H goes into PETS

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
cats and dogs are examples of pets, hence the question mark
h is an abbreviation for hours, taken inside PETS

annotation.surface: Weather forecasters spend hours on the phrase "raining cats and dogs".
annotation.walkthrough: "Cats and dogs" in quotes calls up the heavy-rain saying that weather forecasters use, but here it just means pets.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: those who foretell what is coming, whether seers of old or weather forecasters.
